newsitem.title: GERMANY: PROSECUTORS ASK SIX YEARS, NINE MONTHS FOR GRAF.
newsitem.headline: PROSECUTORS ASK SIX YEARS, NINE MONTHS FOR GRAF.

text.p: German prosecutors demanded six years and nine months jail on Tuesday for the father of world women's tennis number one seed Steffi Graf.
Prosecutors accused Peter Graf of trying to evade 19.2 million marks ($12.10 million) in tax on his daughter's earnings between 1989 und 1993.
They contested that Graf and Eckardt were guilty of five counts of "simple" tax evasion and one count of "serious" evasion.
Graf's defence is due to make a closing statement in the next few days.
The court, under German procedures, must then decide on a verdict and, if the verdict is guilty, a sentence. The verdict is expected on January 24.
Prosecutors demanded four years and nine months in jail for Graf's former tax adviser Joachim Eckardt, who has also been on trial in the court in Mannheim since the beginning of September last year.
